mappings.note: Lens formula for v, then m = v/u for image size and nature - LO-3's 'applies the lens formula'. The dioptre definition in part (a) has no outcome of its own.
Lens type chosen from required image characteristics and justified by three constructions. No numbers, so the competency covers the identification and C 8.1-LO-2 the drawing.
Single clean lens-formula substitution for position, then magnification for size. Nothing qualitative and nothing drawn.
Lens type from the image being caught on a screen, f from the lens formula, then power and image size - the lens-formula clause carries the item; power is the unnamed extra.
Part (i) names the two standard construction rays and demands the diagram - exactly C 8.1-LO-2; part (ii) is a separate mirror-formula/magnification calculation.
Mirror identified from invariant image characteristics plus a diagram; the third code is for R = +24 cm, where the sign alone decides the mirror is convex - a sign-convention reading, not arithmetic.
Each case is settled by computing R = 2f and comparing it with u (LO-2), then naming the image characteristics (LO-1); mirror C additionally requires a ray diagram.
Same R = 2f comparison and characteristics, but no diagram is demanded here - that is the only thing separating it from its twin case study. Near-duplicate; see defect list.
Built entirely on the magnification formula: nature from the sign, v = 3x from m = -v/u, and the mirror formula written in terms of R. LO-2 covers both named formulae.
Distinguishing concave from convex lenses by the image seen is a lens-property judgement (competency); the m = +0.75 reading and the power passage are the nearest LO-3 content.
What changes on refraction (wavelength and velocity, not frequency), bending into glass, and v from n = c/v - all three sub-parts are the laws of refraction and the definition of n.
Rear-view convex mirror image type and field of view, asked three ways. Purely image characteristics; no formula, no diagram, no refraction.
Ranks two lenses by power from their thickness and prescribes for a vision defect - power is the graded quantity (nearest code LO-3) over a base of converging/diverging lens properties.
Finds f from the u = v observation, orders image distances against object distances, and quotes the 4f minimum - lens-position reasoning, LO-3. Answer key is unsound; see defect list.

Reads the standard convex-lens table for image position and nature, then a lens-formula substitution for f. LO-3 covers both the table reading and the calculation. Sub-part (iv) data is inconsistent; see defect list.
R = 2f, the small-aperture condition and the focus lying midway between P and C - the mirror geometry LO-1's image location depends on. Nothing is substituted, so not LO-2.
Optically rarer and denser defined by speed, and everyday raised-bottom and raised-letter effects - the laws of refraction, LO-3. No lens or lens formula appears.

The passage sets the pole as origin and the principal axis as the x-axis - the ray-optics-to-coordinates link that is exactly C 5.3-LO-1 - and the questions then turn on the magnification formula and its sign.
Naming the magnifier and drawing the very-enlarged virtual-image construction. The diagram is the graded product; the lens/mirror identification rests on lens properties.
Fairground mirror read as concave over convex from which half is enlarged and which diminished - image characteristics by mirror type, no formula and no diagram.

Explicitly 'without doing any calculations': f is inferred from the u = v row and the bad row is spotted by the real/virtual rule. Still LO-3's lens-position reasoning, applied to data rather than to one substitution.
